topic.subject: physics
topic.title: Light, reflection and refraction
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26: Light and the Eye; TGS 2026-27: Waves 2
topic.overview: Ray models describe how light travels, reflects from surfaces and changes direction at boundaries between transparent materials.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Light travels in straight lines through a uniform medium and can travel through a vacuum.
We see a non-luminous object when light from a source reflects from it into the eye.
Angles in reflection are measured from the normal, not the mirror surface.
The law of reflection is angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
Refraction is a change in direction caused by a change in wave speed at a boundary.
Light usually bends towards the normal when it slows on entering a more optically dense medium and away when it speeds up on leaving.
A fair refraction test controls block material/shape and wavelength while varying incidence angle.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: a line showing the direction in which light travels
an imaginary line at 90 degrees to a surface
angle between incoming ray and normal
angle between reflected ray and normal
change in direction when light changes speed at a boundary
allowing light through so objects can be seen clearly

workedExamples.prompt: Incidence angle is 38 degrees. Find reflection angle.
Light enters glass from air and slows. State bending direction.
workedExamples.answer: Towards the normal, unless it enters exactly along the normal.

practicals.title: Reflection and refraction ray tracing
practicals.variables: IV: angle of incidence; DV: reflected/refracted angle; controls: material, block orientation and light colour.
practicals.method: Draw around apparatus, use a narrow ray, mark ray points, remove apparatus, join points with a ruler, draw normal and measure from it; repeat angles.
practicals.expectedResult: Reflection angles match within uncertainty; refraction angle changes systematically with incidence angle.
practicals.safety: Use a ray box safely, keep light away from eyes and handle glass blocks carefully.
practicals.evaluation: Use widely spaced points, thin lines, a sharp pencil, repeated angle readings and avoid moving the block.

commonMistakes: Measuring angles from the mirror instead of the normal.
Saying the eye sends rays to an object.
Saying light bends because it reaches the boundary at a different colour only.
examTips: Use arrows to show ray direction.
For refraction, name both the speed change and bending direction.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.subject: physics
practicals.title: Reflection and refraction ray tracing
practicals.variables: IV: angle of incidence; DV: reflected/refracted angle; controls: material, block orientation and light colour.
practicals.method: Draw around apparatus, use a narrow ray, mark ray points, remove apparatus, join points with a ruler, draw normal and measure from it; repeat angles.
practicals.expectedResult: Reflection angles match within uncertainty; refraction angle changes systematically with incidence angle.
practicals.safety: Use a ray box safely, keep light away from eyes and handle glass blocks carefully.
practicals.evaluation: Use widely spaced points, thin lines, a sharp pencil, repeated angle readings and avoid moving the block.
